reasons: The code is short and clear, but no tests are visible.
The startup log uses fixed list positions to name providers, so reordering the list breaks the labels.
The warning says RSS will activate once sources are seeded, but the RSS provider always reports itself as available, so the wording may mislead.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and shared slot
sections.what: Brings in the router, the four providers, the storage module, and the router type, and sets up an empty slot to hold the one shared router.
sections.why: Likely reason: the empty slot is what makes the router a single shared instance.

sections.name: createSearchRouter
sections.title: Building the router once
sections.what: Creates the four providers, logs which have keys set and which are available now, warns if none are available, and returns the new router. Later calls reuse it.
sections.why: Likely reason: the warning explains why results may be few when no keys are set.
sections.watch_out: The startup log is a snapshot; the router rechecks providers on every search.

sections.name: getSearchRouter
sections.title: Getting the shared router
sections.what: Returns the existing shared router, or builds it first if none exists yet.
sections.why: Likely reason: callers can ask for the router from anywhere without worrying about startup order.

summary: Builds one shared search router that combines the search providers, and hands the same router to any part of the app that asks for it.
purpose: Creates the list of search providers and the router that uses them, once, and logs which providers are active.
why: Likely reason: one shared router avoids rebuilding providers for every search.
how: On the first call, it builds the Tavily, SearchAPI, SerpAPI, and RSS providers, checks which ones are set up, logs the result, warns if none are, and creates the router with a function that loads enabled sources. Later calls return the same router.
inputs: Environment settings for each provider's keys, and the source list loaded from storage.
outputs: A router object with a search method, plus startup log lines about which providers are active.
risks: Providers are built once, so the list does not change while the process runs. With no keys, the app runs on RSS alone and the warning may be easy to miss. The startup log reads providers by fixed position, so reordering the list mislabels them.
debug: If results are thin, read the search-router startup lines to see which providers were active. After adding a key, restart the server, because the startup log is a snapshot. The router rechecks availability on each search.
